title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
summary: A guide to software craftsmanship covering topics from personal responsibility and career development to architectural techniques for keeping code flexible and easy to adapt.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
summary: A novel set in the American South during the 1930s, exploring themes of racial injustice and moral growth through the eyes of young Scout Finch.

author: George Orwell
summary: A dystopian novel depicting a totalitarian society under constant surveillance, where independent thinking is persecuted as thoughtcrime.

title: JavaScript: The Good Parts
author: Douglas Crockford
summary: A concise exploration of the most reliable and useful parts of JavaScript, filtering out the features that are less well thought out.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
summary: A sweeping narrative of human history from the Stone Age to the present, examining how biology and history have defined what it means to be human.

title: Domain-Driven Design
author: Eric Evans
summary: A framework for making design decisions and a vocabulary for discussing design in the context of complex software systems aligned with business domains.

title: To Kill a Kingdom
author: Alexandra Christo
summary: A dark fantasy retelling of The Little Mermaid where a siren princess who collects the hearts of princes meets a prince determined to destroy her.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
summary: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship presenting principles, patterns, and practices of writing clean, readable, and maintainable code.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
summary: A coming-of-age story narrated by teenager Holden Caulfield as he wanders New York City after being expelled from prep school.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
summary: An exploration of the two systems that drive the way we think—fast intuitive thinking and slow deliberate thinking—and how they shape our judgements and decisions.

title: Design Patterns
author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides
summary: The classic catalogue of 23 object-oriented design patterns that provide reusable solutions to common software design problems.

title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
summary: An accessible and entertaining journey through the story of science, from the Big Bang to the rise of civilisation, explaining complex concepts in plain language.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
summary: A sweeping multi-generational saga of the Buendía family in the fictional town of Macondo, blending magical realism with Colombian history.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
summary: A comprehensive guide to the principles and practicalities of data systems, covering databases, stream processing, batch processing, and distributed architectures.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
summary: A dystopian novel set in a future World State where citizens are genetically engineered, socially conditioned, and pacified by a pleasure drug called soma.
